title: `width: -webkit-fill-available;` is removed unexpectedly
impact: 2 reactions, 2 reporters (Vite cssMinify with build.target 'esnext', which per the reporter passes targets: {}; unplugin-lightningcss). Only users who give no browser targets are affected. The maintainer said in Dec 2024 that this works as expected.
code: src/properties/size.rs: SizeHandler::handle_property (property! macro flushes the previous value only when targets.browsers is Some and the new value is incompatible)
src/properties/size.rs: Size/MaxSize::is_compatible (MinContent/MaxContent/FitContent ignore the vendor prefix)
summary: With no targets, Lightning CSS assumes a browser with full standards support, so `width:-webkit-fill-available;width:-moz-available;width:stretch` collapses to `width:stretch` (last declaration wins). With real targets (e.g. browserslist 'defaults' or '>= 0.25%') all three are kept, and a lone `-webkit-fill-available` is never removed. Two smaller bugs turned up in the same handler: two *different* prefixed values collapse to the last one (e.g. `-webkit-fill-available;-moz-available` -> `-moz-available` without targets, and `-webkit-max-content;-moz-max-content` -> `-moz-max-content` even with targets), which breaks Chromium/WebKit.
repro: 826-repro.mjs (+ 826-repro-prefixes.mjs for the #1371 crash). Reporter's case, targets {}: `.a{width:-webkit-fill-available;width:-moz-available;width:stretch}` -> `.a{width:stretch}`; with browserslist 'defaults' -> all three kept. Side bugs: `.a{width:-webkit-fill-available;width:-moz-available}` (no targets) -> `.a{width:-moz-available}`; `.a{width:-webkit-max-content;width:-moz-max-content}` (defaults) -> `.a{width:-moz-max-content}`.
evidence: Local master and 1.27.0, 1.30.2 (same outputs; 1.31.1-1.33.0 also). Targets compared: none, {}, '>= 0.25%', 'defaults', chrome 120, safari 17, firefox 120. equivalence.mjs (Chrome 153, simple flex/inline-block fixture): webkit+moz -> moz NOT EQUIVALENT (span width 300px -> 12.45px); webkit-max-content+moz -> moz NOT EQUIVALENT; all3 -> stretch EQUIVALENT in Chrome; `height:100vh;height:-webkit-fill-available` -> fill-available only EQUIVALENT in Chrome. Compat data (src/compat.rs): StretchSize Chrome 138+, Safari 27+, no Firefox; so the no-targets `stretch`-only output only works in Chromium 138+ today. Also found: `include: Features.VendorPrefixes` on `width: stretch` without targets panics (`unreachable!` in size.rs) in every release 1.22.0-1.33.0; this is #1371, fixed on master by 9d0da3f (#1377), not yet released. It may be what fregante hit.

fix.approach: For the side bugs (optional, separate issue): in SizeHandler's property! macro, also flush when the stored and incoming values are the same keyword with different vendor prefixes (Stretch/MinContent/MaxContent/FitContent), independent of targets; and make is_compatible take the prefix into account for the *-content keywords. The no-targets collapse itself is the documented model and stays.

subcases.case: no targets: prefixed + standard collapse to standard
subcases.note: maintainer comment 2024-12-08; fix is to pass targets

subcases.case: two different prefixed values collapse to the last (fill-available, *-content)
subcases.note: unrealistic without the unprefixed value in autoprefixer-style output, but silently breaks Chromium/WebKit; suggest tracking separately or closing as fringe

draftReply:
This is expected when no browser targets are given: Lightning CSS then assumes a browser with full standards support and drops vendor-prefixed fallbacks, so `width: -webkit-fill-available; width: -moz-available; width: stretch` becomes `width: stretch`. With real targets all three are kept, e.g. `targets: browserslistToTargets(browserslist('defaults'))` gives `width:-webkit-fill-available;width:-moz-available;width:stretch`, and a lone `-webkit-fill-available` is never removed.

In Vite, `build.target: 'esnext'` ends up passing empty targets when minifying CSS, as you found. Setting `build.cssTarget` to real browsers (for example `['chrome111', 'safari16', 'firefox115']`) should keep the fallbacks.

Separately, `include: Features.VendorPrefixes` with `stretch` and no targets currently crashes in released versions (#1371). That's fixed on master and will be in the next release.
